blocks.text: Draft for Jared's approval. Built only from the monthly MLS® figures (SnapStats) for condos and townhomes in Capitol Hill. No local notes, sold prices, building list or live listing feed yet; see the open items.

Capitol Hill, Burnaby: 19 condos and townhomes listed at the end of October 2026 and 1 sold in the month, a sales ratio of 5%, which the reports’ scale reads as a buyers’ market. By listings that is number 13 of 35 Burnaby communities for condos and townhomes.

blocks.source: Source: MLS® data from the Greater Vancouver REALTORS® and the Fraser Valley Real Estate Board, compiled by SnapStats®. Sales ratio is homes sold divided by homes listed. On the reports’ own scale under 12% is a buyers’ market, 12% to 20% is balanced and over 20% is a sellers’ market. With fewer than ten homes listed, one sale moves the ratio a long way, so treat it as a rough signal. The reports count condos and townhomes together in one line, so this table cannot separate the two. Shares are this community’s count divided by the Burnaby total for condos and townhomes that month.

blocks.text: Listings of condos and townhomes in Capitol Hill rose from 16 in June to 19 in October (+18.8%), and 7 sold across the 5 months. In October the community held 1.5% of Burnaby’s 1,309 condos and townhomes listed.
Condos and townhomes or houses in Capitol Hill?

blocks.text: Capitol Hill Condos and Townhomes: streets and boundaries

items.t: Capitol Hill's condo and townhome stock sits on and below Hastings Street, not on the hilltop house streets: the City's major-projects list places the area's one current strata project under the Hastings plan area at 4472 Hastings Street, at Willingdon Avenue.

The neighbourhood's heritage anchor is the Capitol Hill Community Hall, built in 1947–1948 on a triangular lot in Dynes Park beside Hastings Street at the terminus of the former Hastings streetcar line, per the City's Heritage Burnaby record.

blocks.text: Capitol Hill Condos and Townhomes: the housing stock

items.t: The attached stock here is small and ground-oriented compared with Burnaby's town centres: the only strata project on the City's current major-projects list for this area is a five-storey mixed-use building at 4472 Hastings Street with 34 strata homes over ground-floor retail (3 studio, 4 one-bedroom, 12 one-bedroom-plus-den including adaptable units, and 15 two-bedroom homes including adaptable units, by the City's unit count).
That 4472 Hastings Street project, by Capitol Hill (4472 Hastings) Ltd. Partnership, is the form this page's new supply takes: low-rise strata over retail at the Willingdon corner, not a tower.

blocks.text: Capitol Hill Condos and Townhomes: rules that affect buyers

items.t: New multi-family buildings in Burnaby are judged under the Burnaby Zoning Bylaw 2026 (Bylaw No. 14815), whose district list separates a Townhouse District (R2) from Low-Rise Apartment (R3, R4), Mid-Rise Apartment (R5, R6) and High-Rise Apartment (R7, R8) districts — so a Hastings Street low-rise and an Ellesmere Avenue townhouse sit in different districts with different rules.

A strata rental-restriction bylaw cannot be enforced here: the Province states that as of November 24, 2022 no strata corporation may have a residential rental-restriction bylaw, all such bylaws are invalid, and only a 55-or-older age-restriction bylaw is allowed; short-term rental bylaws are still allowed.

The same provincial page states that from November 1, 2023 a strata must contribute a minimum of 10% of its annual operating fund to the contingency reserve fund (CRF) when it approves its budget — the figure to check on the Form B of any small Hastings Street strata.

blocks.text: Capitol Hill Condos and Townhomes: local details a buyer would not know

items.t: The R2 extension changed this page's transit on a specific date: TransLink states the extended R2 began September 7, 2026, runs 5 a.m. to 2 a.m. seven days a week, every 6 to 7 minutes at peak and every 10 to 15 minutes off-peak, and replaced the peak-only 222 Willingdon Express.

The hill's community hall predates every strata here: Heritage Burnaby records the Capitol Hill Community Hall as built in 1947–1948 as a non-partisan public space, on a triangular lot in Dynes Park named for William Dynes, the hall association member who was foreman of its construction.

A second City-listed project touches the neighbourhood's east side: a non-market senior citizens and non-market rental development proposed at 6005 Pandora Street (rezoning REZ #21-14, architect Ankenman Marchand), recorded at Initial Report on June 14, 2021 — rental, not strata, so it adds neighbours, not competing condos.

blocks.text: Capitol Hill Condos and Townhomes: costs and taxes

items.t: The City's 2026–2030 Financial Plan raised sewer charges about $14 for a condo (3.5%) and held water at 0%, figures the City states in its January 28, 2026 financial-plan release.

blocks.text: Capitol Hill Condos and Townhomes: getting around

items.t: Hastings Street carries two RapidBus routes past this page's buildings: the R5 Hastings Street (Burrard Station to SFU) and, since September 7, 2026, the R2 Marine–Willingdon (Park Royal to Metrotown Station).

TransLink states the R2 extension improves connections to Burnaby Heights, Brentwood Town Centre, the British Columbia Institute of Technology (BCIT) and Metrotown, and that route 130 continues as the local Willingdon service with most trips terminating at Kootenay Loop.

blocks.text: Capitol Hill Condos and Townhomes: risks and due diligence

items.t: Slope is this page's lot-level check: Capitol Hill's strata buildings sit on or below a steep hill, and the Zoning Bylaw 2026's Form and Character Development Permit Area guidelines are the document that governs multi-family form and character — a buyer of a hillside townhouse should confirm whether the lot is in a development permit area on the City's zoning map before relying on a renovation plan.

For any strata purchase, read the depreciation report cycle: the Province's strata legislation page tracks the updated depreciation report requirements effective July 1, 2024, and the October 27, 2025 expansion of who may prepare them — a small strata's report date is a Form B question, not a listing fact.

blocks.text: Capitol Hill home prices: what sold, November 2025 to October 2026

15 condos sold in Capitol Hill with a median price of $617,500 (the middle half sold between $496,500 and $856,500), taking a median of 48 days to sell at 97.5% of the last list price; 33% sold above list. They had a median $799 per square foot, a median year built of 2012 and a median strata fee of $550 a month.

faq.q: How many condos and townhomes are for sale in Capitol Hill?
faq.a: At the end of October 2026 the Greater Vancouver REALTORS® figures showed 19 condos and townhomes listed in Capitol Hill. That is a month-end count and it moves daily; ask Jared what is on the market today.

faq.q: Is Capitol Hill a buyers’ or sellers’ market for condos and townhomes?
faq.a: In October 2026, condos and townhomes in Capitol Hill had a sales ratio of 5%, which the reports’ scale reads as a buyers’ market. On the reports’ scale under 12% favours buyers, 12% to 20% is balanced and over 20% favours sellers.

faq.q: How many condos and townhomes sold in Capitol Hill from June to October 2026?
faq.a: 7 condos and townhomes sold in Capitol Hill over those 5 months, out of 916 in all of Burnaby.

faq.q: Do these numbers separate condos from townhomes?
faq.a: No. The monthly reports publish condos and townhomes as one line, so every count here includes both. Jared can pull the split for a specific building or street.

faq.q: What did condos in Capitol Hill sell for?
faq.a: 15 condos sold in Capitol Hill between November 1, 2025 to October 22, 2026, with a median price of $617,500.

faq.q: How long do condos take to sell in Capitol Hill?
faq.a: The median was 48 days from listing to sale, and homes sold at a median 97.5% of the last list price (33% sold above list), for sales November 1, 2025 to October 22, 2026.
